Comments: ¿In an effort to prevent the spread of the COVID-19 virus, the Department has conducted this administrative inspection in response to information provided by Chief. Code §78a.73(b), §78a81(a)(2) and (3), and §78a.85(a)(5) have been cited. Please note that a violation of 25 Pa. Code §78a.86 was previously cited for this well on 8/23/2019 (Inspection Record #2926839). properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TIMBERLINE ENERGY INC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 10/31/2024
Violation Code: OGA3211(H) - WELL PERMITS - LABELING - Failure to install, in a permanent manner, the permit number on a completed well.
Violation ID: 8206593
Permit API: 031-24689
Unconventional: No
County: Clarion
Municipality: Porter Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/31/2024
Comments: This site located in a vegetated, brushy field west off Miller Road across unnamed tributary to Leatherwood creek on north branch of access road. Well set-up for production with a pump jack, meter and two tanks with no secondary containment. Electronic production reporting submitted through August 2024 with comment "Sell gas into Gourley pipeline system". Tanks are empty, stone around tanks is saturated with oily produced fluid. An NOV was issued on 10/3/24 with violations for the release of less than 30 gallons of produced fluid to ground, no well tag/site sign, and a violation for the unusable state of the bridge.Operator, Jack Cochran contacted WQS Taylor on 10/10/24, he stated that he had contacted Gourleys about posting a well tag/sign and doing a clean-up at this site. He also stated he did not plan to fix the bridge that it was the landowners responsibility to put a deck on the bridge. WQS Taylor has had no contact with Mr. Cochran beyond the call on 10/10/24. There has been no change at this site, well tag/site sign not posted, release of produced fluid from tanks remains and the bridge has not been repaired. Violations issued on 10/3/2024 for the release of produced water from tanks set on site with no secondary containment and for no well tag and no site sign at this site are continued with this inspection.The bridge over the stream remains as it was with rotten boards on the deck, not accessible by vehicle, violation for the bridge continued from a violation issued on 10/17/2017.After review of Department records, it was discovered that General Permit # GP71607601 has been issued to Timberline Energy regarding this stream crossing. Further enforcement action associated with compliance with the issued General Permit may be necessary.

Report Details

Violation ID: 8270767
Permit API: 129-24245
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Derry Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/09/2026
Comments: On April 9 2026, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the Ackerman 2 OG Well. This well is under Consent Order and Agreement (COA) 407094. The well was reportedly plugged on 2/27/2025, therefore the site shall be restored no later than 11/27/2025.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department was unable to locate a restoration plan onsite. Therefore, the Department was unable to compare the well site to the restoration plan, however, the Department was able to assess the access road and well site for permanent stabilization and vegetative growth.Upon inspection of the access road, it appeared to have achieved 70% uniform and adequate vegetative coverage. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed at the time of the inspection.Upon inspection of the former well site, the Department observed an above ground monument for the reportedly plugged well. No other production equipment was observed on site. There were no observed leaks at the surface in the area surrounding the well monument. The well site did not appear to have achieved 70% uniform and adequate vegetative coverage (photo 4). The Department did not observe any erosion and sedimentation controls installed on site. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed at the time of the inspection.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to have E and S controls installed as well as failure to have an E and S plan onsite.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 944665
Permit API: 015-23116
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Columbia Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/09/2022
Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of Repsol's VanBlarcom R 03-113 well site located in Columbia Township, Bradford County on 2/9/2022 at 1025 hours. The weather was 34 degrees with partly cloudy skies. This inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by the operator. Complaint ID #362029 is tied to the release within CTS. On 2/6/2022 at approximately 1500 hours a release of approximately 15 gallons of produced water and 3 gallons of glycol were released to the pad surface. A leaking produced water flow-line released the produced water directly beneath where the leak occurred. Insulation on the flow-line contained the released to the small area beneath the line. The release on the produced water flow-line caused a crack on a pex pipe near the GPU unit which released the glycol to the pad surface. Both areas were observed today having snow, ice and slush removed from the pad surface. It appears as though the snow absorbed the majority of the releases. I collected some snow beneath the produced water flow-line and allowed it to melt. The melted snow was field measured at ~155us/cm. The releases are both cleaned up to visible (photos #5 & 6). Barrels containing the impacted material were observed in the GPU secondary containment (photo #4). I spoke with Mark Watson (Repsol) over the phone while I was onsite. He explained that a leaking pipe on the produced water flow-line caused fluid to kick back, cracking a pex pipe on the GPU. The leaking produced water flow-line was reported to release ~15 gallons of produced water to the pad surface. The cracked pex pipe was reported to release ~3 gallons of glycol to the pad surface. Both areas were reported to be cleaned up to visible. Golder (environmental consultant) screened the areas on 2/7/2022, confirming that the releases had been remediated. I also spoke with Megan Depew (Repsol) over the phone who explained that the areas were hard to access for heavier equipment to excavate so the remediation work was conducted by hand. All impacted snow/ice/slush was placed into barrels and placed on secondary containment awaiting disposal. Based on the findings of today's inspection and Repsol's timely reporting and remediation of the releases, violations of the following are cited as immediately corrected against API # 015-23116: 35 P.S. 691.402(b) 25 Pa. Code 78a.57(a) 35 P.S. 6018.301 I departed the site at 1200 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: COTERRA ENERGY INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78a73(b) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to prevent gas, oil, brine, completion and servicing fluids, and any other fluids or materials from below the casing seat from entering fresh groundwater, and prevent pollution or diminution of fresh groundwater.
Violation ID: 8246141
Permit API: 115-22555
Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Auburn Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/21/2025
Comments: On site today to perform a routine inspection, 72 degs. and cloudy. - There were eight wells on site, all are set up for automated production, they are the Powers M 1H, 2H, 4H, 6H, 8H, 10H, 12H, 14H. The 2H, 8H and the 12H wells have the (20x13), (13x9) and the (9x5) annuli shut in before the common vent line and are set up with ALICAT annular flow monitoring equipment. The 1H, 4H, 6H, 10H and 14H (20x13), (13x9) and (9x5) annuli are open and venting to shared poly tanks. - The cellars had water in them at various heights with no active bubbling noted (see individual inspection reports for particular details of each well on the pad). Comments: On April 13 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the CFR USX 5 OG Well in regards to violations issued under inspection report 4157445. Accompanying me in today's inspection is Rosie Wise (PaDEP)The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department again observed the water flowing onto the access road. It did not appear any remedial actions have been taken to address the flowing water and resulting erosion and sedimentation issues on the access road.As previously described in IR 4157445:The water was observed flowing down the access road where it appeared to end at the well site. Erosion channels appear to have formed along the access road as a result of the flowing water. The water appears to be originating from a drainage channel/tributary to Antram Run. It appears that a culvert located under the access road may be damaged or obstructed, causing the water to flow onto the access road rather than through the culvert. The Department was unable to locate/inspect the culvert inlet. However, no water was observed discharging from the culvert outlet.Upon inspection of the well posting, it appeared a new well posting has been installed on a piece of the production equipment in accordance with OGA3211(H). The well posting appeared to contain the well permit number, operator's name, and operator's phone number. However, it did not appear to contain the operator's address. The Department recommends the operator ensure all required information is properly posted in accordance with OGA3211(G).Based on today's inspection, OGA3211(H) is being closed. All other violations issued in IR 4157445 remain outstanding.

Violation ID: 990919
Permit API: 015-23733
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Springfield Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/06/2023
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection of Blackhill Energy's Jackson A well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 4/6/2023 at 1430 hours. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by Blackhill. Complaint Tracking System (CTS) ID #371191 is tied to this release within CTS. On 4/6/2023 at ~1300 hours an initial estimate of 4 barrels of produced water was discovered by Blackhill Energy to have been released from the produced water offload area at the Jackson pad. Prior to my arrival, the estimate was increased to a potential 7 barrels of produced water. The release occurred when the offload valve for the produced water tanks was not closed all the way after offloading. The valve is held in a yellow bin and the produced water was discovered to be leaking from the bin shown in photo #2. As it leaked from the bin, part of the release was contained to secondary containment and part of the release was spilled to the pad surface. During my inspection, fluids located on the pad surface in the known impacted area from the release were field measured at >19.99mS/cm (photos #1 and 2). After inspecting the rock-lined conveyance channel located just west of the release area (photo #4) it was discovered that elevated conductivity fluids were located in the channel. I field measured fluids in the rock-lined conveyance channel along the entirety of the southern edge of the pad. All fluids in the rock-lined channel up to the stormwater control basin were field measured at >19.99mS/cm. Fluid flowing in the rock-lined channel was observed entering the stormwater control basin. I collected a sample (0983-377) for standard analysis code 942 from the fluid located in the rock-lined conveyance channel just before entering the stormwater control basin (photo #11). This fluid was field measured at >19.99mS/cm (photo #10). Two sumps were constructed along the rock-lined channel to begin collecting any fluids flowing in the channel. The DEP requested that the now impacted stormwater contained in the stormwater basin be collected as a regulated substance due to the release impacting it. As I departed a crew were working on excavating the impacted pad material near the point of release and recovering the fluids that were on the surface of the pad. Temporary storage containers were scheduled to be brought in to be staged onsite for storage of the stormwater control basin's water. Plans to move the produced water tanks and associated secondary containment to begin excavating beneath it were also being made. The drain pipe of the stormwater basin was believed to be clogged but was also closed as a precaution. I departed the site at 1600 hours. Based on the reported release of produced water outside of containment and the discovery of the release entering conveyance channels and reaching the stormwater controls, violations of the following are cited against API #015-23733: 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)35 P.S. 6018.30135 P.S. 691.402(b)

Comments: On 3/30/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Grippo well site. It was 25 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. Water/ice puddles from recent rain/snowfall were scattered across the pad surface. I field tested some of these with an Oakton PCTS 50 for conductivity and discovered a 60' x 60' ice/water puddle southeast of the wellheads and adjacent to the south edge of the secondary containment for six frac tanks that field tested at 4.05 mS conductance. Sample 9551-049 was collected from this puddle. Two water puddles between the two frac tank secondary containments field tested at 1.5 mS conductance. Other water puddles tested at less than 0.6 mS conductance. I discussed the elevated conductance fluids with Chesapeake's Kyle Stephens. He directed an arriving vac truck to start sucking up the fluids. No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. Temporary stabilization has been applied to the perimeter berm. PCSM is addressed by three retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed. Temporary compost filter socks remain in place down slope from the infiltration areas.There were five wells staged for flowback/production. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The production tank had secondary containment. There were six frac tanks in secondary containment that were connected to the wellheads. There were 10 frac tanks on the north side of location that were stationed in secondary containment but were not connected to the well heads at the time of the inspection.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3517519 for high conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface while cleaning up after fracking operations were completed and for elevated conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface during drilling operations.The release of a large volume of elevated conductance fluid to the unprotected pad surface is a violation of CSL 402[b)The DEP recommends the following:1. Because of the elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 due to the unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid impacting the unprotected pad surface.2. Continue to monitor the areas with temporary stabilization and apply addition resources as necessary to achieve at least 70% uniform perennial vegetation.I left the site at 1010 hours.

Violation ID: 990007

Comments: On 3/30/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Grippo well site. It was 25 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. Water/ice puddles from recent rain/snowfall were scattered across the pad surface. I field tested some of these with an Oakton PCTS 50 for conductivity and discovered a 60' x 60' ice/water puddle southeast of the wellheads and adjacent to the south edge of the secondary containment for six frac tanks that field tested at 4.05 mS conductance. Sample 9551-049 was collected from this puddle. Two water puddles between the two frac tank secondary containments field tested at 1.5 mS conductance. Comments Afton Sterling, Regulatory Supervisor of SWN, contacted Scott Kuchta, DEP O&G WQS at 9:40 AM on 8/5/16 to report a diesel fuel spill of an estimated (750) gallons to secondary containment that occurred on 8/5/16 at 5:30 AM. Southwestern Energy submitted a drilling resumption notice to the Department on 7/31/16 indicating that Southwestern Drilling Company Rig #45 will be re-entering the Cramer 2H at 18:00 hours on 8/1/16. Mr. Kuchta and I arrived at the site at 12:00 to conduct an investigation of the incident. SDC #45 is currently in the process of drilling the Cramer 2H well. This was a re-entry of the well. The well had been drilled to kick off point. The horizontal section of the well will be drilled to total depth with a mixture of diesel fuel and synthetic oil based mud. Initially, we met with Mike Deming, Senior Regulatory Analyst of SWN at the entrance gate to the site. We briefly discussed the incident prior to visually assessing it. Mr. Deming stated the following. “The spill volume has been revised from (750) to (375) gallons. The spill was reported to PADEP Northeast Regional Office in Wilkes-Barre, PA at 6:45 AM. An O-ring failed on a generator causing diesel fuel to leak onto the New Park rig mats. The diesel flowed through the seams in the mats, to the containment liner and felt beneath the mats, eventually to the ground due to a breached seam or hole in the liner. Upon completion of our discussion, we walked over to the area on the well pad where the spill occurred in order to assess the incident. Additional SWN personnel accompanying the Department during the inspection included Ms. Sterling, John Hughes, Drilling Superintendent of SWN, Dan Hesserdorfer, site company man of SWN, Justin Phillips, Health, Safety, and Environmental Supervisor of SWN, and Diego Nuila, Regulatory Analyst, of SWN. Based on our observations, it turns out that the spill was not completely contained as originally reported. We observed pools of red dyed diesel fuel with an odor present, on the pad surface in between a frac tank containing fresh water used for cementing of the wells and a frac tank which is used for rig and coolant water according to SWN. Apparently, the liner had been removed to assess the ground surface beneath it. There is also staining observed on the liner and felt. There are pools of diesel fuel on containment and in openings in the rig mats near the generators. There are also white colored absorbent pads on containment used in attempt to contain the spill. There is a petroleum sheen observed on the pad surface next to the containment berm near the generators. It appears that the diesel fuel is emanating from under the containment. The result of the release according to Mr. Hughes was an O-ring failing on a ray core filter system on a generator, which filters diesel fuel coming into the engine of the generator. Mr. Hughes stated that the generators are used to power the rig and rig equipment and this is not the diesel fuel mixed with synthetic oil based mud that is used for drilling purposes. Apparently, the diesel fuel flowed out of the generator onto the rig mats and in between the wedges/seams of the mats. The containment below the mats either has compromised integrity or gaps in between the seams.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/27/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 999886
Permit API: 015-21707
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Franklin Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/28/2023
Comments: Incident Inspection of Chesapeake's "Sensinger" Marcellus well site.Eric Hottenstein (Chesapeake) called the DEP yesterday (June 27, 2023) to report an estimated 20 barrel release of production liquid to the pad surface.I spoke with Eric Hottenstein by phone during this inspection. He explained the following: on June 18, 2023 a vac truck was removing liquid from the production tank. Apparently when the truck left, the valve on the tank was not fully closed, and the camlock plug did not seal. Yesterday Chesapeake's Well Tender saw liquid dripping from the yellow takeout can attached to the production tank. They were immediately able to get the leak to stop. The detection system on the production tank indicates that 20 barrels of production liquid leaked out of the takeout can during the ~10 days it was leaking. Creston Environmental obtained electrical conductivity readings from soil around the tank which indicated contamination from the leak. Hottenstein also explained the Marcellus well at this site produces Naturally Occurring Radioactive Material (NORM). I used a Ludlum 2241-3 meter with a scintillator probe to detect radioactivity. Background reading was 10 uR/hr. Readings ~1" from the production tank were 50-70 uR/hr. Chesapeake contracted Waste Management to decontaminate the production tank. They plan to remove the tank after decon on Monday July 3, 2023. Excavation of contaminated pad material will commence after tank removal. The production liquid release apparently infiltrated into the pad material around/under the tank. Vegetation immediately surrounding the production tank appears stressed (brown) from the leak. I used a Hanna Groline soil probe to get electrical conductivity readings from pad material surrounding the tank. The meter maxed out at 4.0 mS/cm, indicating contamination from the production liquid.Violations for the production liquid release are cited to the 015-21707 drilling permit. Due to the quantity of the release, cleanup is referred to DEP's Environmental Brownfields Program.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site to comply with 102.22 Permanent Stabilization. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Pooled water on the pad surface in 4 separate puddles has electrical conductivity of 0.21-1.3 mS/cm with an Oakton PCTS5.Air temp 67FJLP

Comments: December 27 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in regards to the spill reported to the Department on 10/20/2023 (CTS: 375673). According to the operator, the spill was approximately 40 barrels of production fluid, released from the valve near the bottom of the production tank. The initial inspection of the spill is documented in IR 3636824. The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the production tank appeared to be removed from the site and it appeared that excavation of the contaminated material had begun. The area of excavation was approximately 30 feet by 30 feet and roughly 5.5 feet in depth. The Department took conductivity readings at the bottom of the excavated area with readings of 0.02mS, 0.12mS, and 0.18mS. It appeared that all of the excavated material was still on site, in several piles surrounding the excavated hole. In some areas, it appeared sediment had begun to travel downslope from the piles. Upon further inspection, it appeared that no E and S BMPs were implemented anywhere on the site. The Department recommends the operator promptly install E and S BMPs to prevent further migration of sediment and to minimize the potential for further sedimentation to occur.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to implement E and S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Previous violations associated with the release remain outstanding.

The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the production tank appeared to be removed from the site and it appeared that excavation of the contaminated material had begun. The area of excavation was approximately 30 feet by 30 feet and roughly 5.5 feet in depth. The Department took conductivity readings at the bottom of the excavated area with readings of 0.02mS, 0.12mS, and 0.18mS. It appeared that all of the excavated material was still on site, in several piles surrounding the excavated hole. In some areas, it appeared sediment had begun to travel downslope from the piles. Upon further inspection, it appeared that no E and S BMPs were implemented anywhere on the site. The Department recommends the operator promptly install E and S BMPs to prevent further migration of sediment and to minimize the potential for further sedimentation to occur.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to implement E and S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Previous violations associated with the release remain outstanding.

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8223193
Permit API: 117-22227
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Covington Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/03/2025
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that a fluid was released from secondary containment on the well pad and it flowed off of the well pad. Upon arriving on location I met with Repsol representative Roy Trimmer. He showed me where the fluid peaked out of the containment, down the pad side slope, and along a vegetated infiltration berm. The secondary containment is present along the west side of the well pad. The secondary containment had previously held a battery of upright tanks containing produced fluid. The tanks have been removed from the location and a crew was working to remove the secondary containment during this inspection. The leak in the containment occurred along the west side of the containment near the southwest corner of the pad. The fluid ran down the west pad side slope near the southwest corner of the pad and along a vegetated, earthen infiltration berm. The fluid ran along the toe of the berm. The berm ends at an infiltration basin. The soil was moist along the path of the fluid. The fluid appeared to stop at the rock-lined entrance to the basin. Fluid present in the infiltration basin near the area of the leak along the west side of the containment had electrical conductivity (EC) readings between 1392 uS/cm to 1500 uS/cm as measured by the Oakton water EC meter. The EC readings in the soil on the Hanna soil EC meter were 2070 uS/cm at the highest not far from the toe of the pad side slope to 250 uS/cm where the path of the fluid ended at the entrance to the infiltration basin. Repsol representative Andrew Senefelder arrived on location during this inspection. He told me that their consultant Resource Environmental would be taking soil samples from the path of the fluid as well as a water sample from inside the secondary containment. He said that due to the EC readings in the soil, they did not anticipate finding any exceedances in the soil; however, as a precaution, Repsol plans to scrape the soil along the flow path of the fluid release anyway, he stated.Mr. Senefelder then left and I took sample 0718-253 from the fluid within the secondary containment near where the leak occurred near the southwest corner of the well pad. The sample was sent to the state laboratory the next day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Al, Sr, and Br.Due to the unknown spill volume, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation. In a phone call with PA DEP Water Quality Specialist Supervisor Sean VanFleet on 3/3/25 at 1600, Repsol representative Kris Perritt committed to pursuing Act 2 remediation for this release. Violations noted.

He told me that their consultant Resource Environmental would be taking soil samples from the path of the fluid as well as a water sample from inside the secondary containment. The sample was sent to the state laboratory the next day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Al, Sr, and Br.Due to the unknown spill volume, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/15/2026 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Brokenstraw Township, Warren county. SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/15/2026
Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 8278408
Permit API: 123-45905
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Brokenstraw Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/15/2026
Comments: A discharge of production fluids is evident at the Conklin Lease tank battery. Mature trees at the southwest corner of the secondary containment area are either heavily stressed or dead. A brine tank is buried within the secondary containment area. PVC lines connect the drain valves of the stock tanks in containment to cutout holes in the surface of the brine tank. Evidence of previous fluid releases in the containment area are visible via crude oil staining and sawdust sprinkled over the oil-stained areas. It appears that the PVC lines connected to the two stock tanks in the southernmost end of the containment area have been the most heavily used. At the time of this inspection, the PVC lines are placed inside the cutout holes of the brine tank. However, oil-staining, visible wetness, and sawdust sprinkled around these cutout holes indicate that at one time fluid was allowed to run over the surface of the brine tank and onto the ground within the secondary containment area. Elevated specific conductance in soils in excess of 3,000 uS/cm was observed beneath both of the aforementioned PVC lines.A pool of fluid was present in the southernmost end of the containment area, in what appeared to be a sump. At the time of this inspection, the fluid was observed to have elevated specific conductance exceeding 4,000 uS/cm. Soils at the bottom of the sump also had elevated specific conductance which measured in excess of 11,000 uS/cm. The floor of the secondary containment area above the sump was found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 2,000 uS/cm. A drainage swale is located approximately 30 feet west of the secondary containment area wall. Upslope soil conductivity readings in the swale were observed at 96 uS/cm. Elevated specific conductance in excess of 4,000 uS/cm was observed in soils within the swale directly across from the tank battery. Crude oil staining was also observed in the swale near the tank battery. The swale transitions to an UNT to Irvine Run with defined bed and banks downslope of the tank battery. The water flowing in the UNT was found to have elevated specific conductance exceeding 13,000 uS/cm. Elevated specific conductance of water was observed throughout the stream at the time of this inspection. The specific conductance of water in the stream was observed to drop below 1,000 uS/cm after two confluences with apparently unaffected sources of fresh water at a point approximately 200 feet north of a culvert and the lease road which crosses the UNT. Because the volume of this release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold, the use of either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required.It is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners provide the Department with brine disposal receipts for the Conklin lease.

Comments: On 04/04/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 Well Site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). On 03/11/2024, the violations were issued as outstanding (IR 3726997). The operator was in compliance with schedule on 03/27/2024 (IR 3736262).The following was observed during inspection on 04/04/2024:Inspection conducted after several large rain events. The beginning upper part of the channel was displaying accelerated erosion and rills entering the channel (Photos 1, 2). The opposite side of the road was displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Sediment accumulation was noted within the stabilized area with establishing vegetation (Photos 3, 4). Upper culvert inlet was blocked with sediment (Photo 5).Several sections of the bank above the channel did not have temporary stabilization. A section of open soils was displaying rills leading into the channel. The channel was also displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation (Photos 6, 7).The middle culvert was completely blocked with sediment. Gravel was noted above the inlet, flowing over towards the channel. Debris and channelization were noted leaving the culvert inlet (Photos 8-10).The outlet of the middle culvert had sediment accumulation within the grass and accelerated erosion below (Photos 11-15).Outlet of roadside channel was displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation. It was noted that sediment and flow were also both coming from the direction of the Landowner's building, in addition to the site's channel. Sediment accumulation within vegetation leading to the collection box and the site's middle culvert (Photos 16-20).Sediment accumulation within culvert and the outlet. This leads towards the stream (Photos 21, 22).Several rills leading off site and towards the roadside channel near the beginning section of the access road (Photos 23, 24). Remnants of gravel/sediment noted leading off the beginning of the access road towards the main township road (Photo 25).The violations issued on 03/11/2024 remain outstanding. A violation of 102.22(b)1 is being issued for the lack of temporary stabilization and the associated accelerated erosion.
